objetive.text: To write short, simple notes, emails and postings to friends. To write dates, and times using digits and words.

1.explanation: During this lesson, students will practice to identify a piece of writing, which uses simple notes, digits and words. If writing dates has you stymied at times, it is probably for one of two reasons. The first is that date formats vary the world over, and we come across these different styles frequently in our reading. The second may be that you aren’t quite sure how to write dates with commas.

objetive.text: Write their names, address and nationality. Write the letters of the alphabet in upper and lower case.

2.explanation: In this lesson students will learn and practice the letters of the alphabet. Also they will identify the correct way to write their names, nationalities or addresses.

objetive.text: Write simple sentences about their and other people´s family and where they live. Spell a range of common names and greetings.

3.explanation: Greetings are nice things to say when people meet each other. Greetings may be different from culture to culture.

objetive.text: Understand, learn and use vocabulary related to days of the week and months of the year.
Understand and use vocabulary related to geography
Understand and use vocabulary related to clothing and style

6.explanation: Clothing is what someone wears to cover their body. Any of a wide variety of articles, usually made of fabrics, animal hair, animal skin, or some combination of them. The wearing of clothing is mainly restricted to human beings and is a characteristic of all human societies. Clothes are used in order to provide a barrier between the skin and the environment.

objetive.text: Analyze and use vocabulary related to family.

7.explanation: Family is a group of individuals who share ties of blood, marriage, or adoption; a group residing together and consisting of parents, children, aunts, uncles, cousins, grandparents and others. Family is also a group of people who share common ancestors

objetive.text: Can recognize the letters of the alphabet
Can understand simple descriptions of people’s physical appearance.
Can use a range of time expressions with whole numbers (+ o’clock)

10.explanation: When we want to express an exact time in English we use the word o’clock after the number. It is important to state that in English we typically do not use the 24-hour time system. In other words, we do not say 16:00 hours, or sixteen hundred hours. We would say 4:00 pm.

objetive.text: Can ask someone’s age using ‘How old’ .....?

11.explanation: When we want to know people’s age we normally use the question How old with the verb to be in present (am-is-are).

objetive.text: Can use subject pronouns with the correct form of the verb ´be´ in the simple present

12.explanation: When using the verb to be and a subject pronoun, we often use contractions. A contraction is created when two words and made into one. Example: I + am = I’m

objetive.text: Can use personal pronouns as objects and complements

13.explanation: Object pronouns are used as complements in the sentences. They are used to represent the person, animal or thing that is the object of a verb or a preposition. For example; Look the picture about the Flintstone family.

21.explanation: Means of transportation is any of the different kinds of transport facilities used for moving goods and people from one location to the other. The means of transportation are bus, train, aeroplane, ship, car, etc while the mode of transportation refers to road, air, sea/ocean, etc.

objetive.text: Identify and use words related to food and drinks

22.explanation: Food, substance consisting essentially of protein, carbohydrate, fat, and other nutrients used in the body of an organism to sustain growth and vital processes and to furnish energy. A drink  is a liquid intended for human consumption. In addition to their basic function of satisfying thirst, drinks play important roles in human culture. Common types of drinks include plain drinking water, milk, coffee, tea, hot chocolate, juice and soft drinks.

objetive.text: Can ask about the price of something using ‘How much is/are?’

23.explanation: How much is and how much are are used to ask about the price of something. How much is is used to ask for a price in singular and how much are is used to ask for a price in plural.

objetive.text: Can use (‘s) to express possession with singular and plural nouns

24.explanation: We use the apostrophe (‘s) to show ownership, belonging to

So it’s really useful to know how to ask for and understand directions in English so you can reach your destination. It’s also great to be able to give directions yourself to tourists or foreign colleagues. So what words and phrases can help you give and ask for directions? Read on to find out! 29.explanation: A body part is a part of an organism such as an organ or extremity.

objetive.text: Understand and use prepositions.

30.explanation: Prepositions of place describe the position of a person or thing in relation to another person or thing.

37.explanation: Prepositions of Place are used to show the position or location of one thing with another.

38.explanation: A subject pronoun is exactly what it sounds like: a pronoun that takes the place of a noun as the subject of a sentence. Remember, a sentence's subject is the person or thing that performs the action of a verb. ... Subject pronouns can be singular or plural, and they can be masculine, feminine, or gender neutral.

objetive.text: Can ask wh-questions using the present simple

39.explanation: Wh- questions are questions that require more information in their answers. Typical wh- words are what, where, when, why, who, how, how many, how much.

objetive.text: Can use the imperative form

40.explanation: Use the imperative form to give instructions, orders and warnings. Must is often used in signs and notices to give instructions.

objetive.text: Can use ‘can’ to refer to ability in the present.

41.explanation: Use can / can’t to talk about your abilities now.

43.explanation: Well, first of all, remember to keep in mind the progressive is only used with ACTION verbs. Another important difference is that we use the simple perfect forms to express finished QUANTITIES and the progressive perfect forms when we are stressing the continuous duration of a specific action mentioned.

objetive.text: Identify and use words related to parts of the house and furniture.

44.explanation: A house is a building for people to live in. It is usually built for a family (parents and their children). Most modern houses have special areas or rooms for people to do the things that they need to live comfortably. A modern house has a place to cook food, a place to eat, places to sleep, a place to wash, also a place to park the car, a place to work and many others. Furniture refers to movable objects intended to support various human activities such as seating (e.g., chairs, stools, and sofas), eating (tables), and sleeping (e.g., beds). Furniture is also used to hold objects at a convenient height for work (as horizontal surfaces above the ground, such as tables and desks), or to store things (e.g., cupboards and shelves). Furniture can be a product of design and is considered a form of decorative art. In addition to furniture's functional role, it can serve a symbolic or religious purpose. It can be made from many materials, including metal, plastic, and wood.

objetive.text: Understand and use connectors to join words and sentences.

45.explanation: Connectors or linkers can help you join two or more ideas (sentences), allowing you to have a more structured and harmonious delivery. Instead of using single sentences, you can connect them in a logical way.

objetive.text: Understand and use vocabulary related to sports.

46.explanation: Sport pertains to any form of competitive physical activity or game that aims to use, maintain or improve physical ability and skills while providing enjoyment to participants and, in some cases, entertainment to spectators. Sports can, through casual or organized participation, improve one's physical health. Hundreds of sports exist, from those between single contestants, through to those with hundreds of simultaneous participants, either in teams or competing as individuals.

53.explanation: Gerund is considered a noun. A noun in English can be a person, place, object or abstract concept, or an activity.

topic.top: HOW INTERESTING IS YOUR ENGLISH CLASS

objetive.text: To ask for information using how + adjective/adverb.

54.explanation: We can use How + adjective/adverb to ask for specific information.

objetive.text: To use SOME and ANY as quantifiers with count and noncount.

55.explanation: ANY is used for questions and negatives while SOME is used for positive. Both may be used with countable and uncountable nouns. SOME may also be used for questions, typically offers and requests, if we think the answer will be positive.

objetive.text: To use was and were with a range of complement phrases.

56.explanation: Was and Were are both past tenses of the verb to be. Was is used in the first person singular (I) and the third person singular (he, she, it) Were is used in the second person singular and plural (you) and first and third person plural (we, they)

objetive.text: To understand the general meaning of short, simple informational material and descriptions if there is visual support.

57.explanation: The following activities are concerned with the use of simple informational material and descriptions, which have the potential to develop communication skills through visual support. The readings have been chosen for their intrinsic interest and their use of target grammar and vocabulary. These types of activities have been carefully selected to develop the confidence of the student when facing them. The activities include comprehension and vocabulary work as well as practicing some readings, such as predictions and basic readings.

objetive.text: To understand simple descriptions of people´s physical appearance.

58.explanation: Physical appearance adjectives in English talk about someone. Students must know the vocabulary related to physical appearance to identify someone visually and be able to describe it in English. For example, in the event that students have to identify a classmate, through the description of the physical appearance, they will be able to find the classmate who is in the classroom. This will also allow the teacher to recognize the student.

objetive.text: To find specific, predictable information in everyday materials (e.g. menus)

59.explanation: This is an activity of reading comprehension where students can learn restaurant terms and they can answer some questions about it. They can say the time, and they can ask some questions and answers with the waiter about food and drinks.

objetive.text: To understand the general meaning of short, simple informational material and descriptions.

60.explanation: This is an activity of reading comprehension where students can talk about sickness and health terms and they can answer some questions about it.They can know some things about medicine, and they can ask some questions to a doctor.

objetive.text: To understand and talk about jobs and occupations.

61.explanation: Job is the work that people do to earn money, especially when they work for a company or public organization. Occupation is used to refer to the kind of work that somebody does. It's used mainly on official forms.

objetive.text: To use vocabulary related to emotions.

62.explanation: Emotion words are used to describe specific emotions. Learning the words for feelings and emotions through pictures can help students better understand feelings and express them correctly. The characters' facial expressions and body movement are very helpful for students to understand these new words. These words help students to recognize their own emotions and at the same time put them into practice to communicate with other students.

objetive.text: To use vocabulary related to emotions.

63.explanation: We use quantifiers when we want to give someone information about the number of something.

objetive.text: To understand and use words related to the learning environment.

64.explanation: This group of words will help students to learn new words and ideas, and they can be a really effective way to show complex or challenging new information. They also help students to order and organize information and ideas. This can be useful before writing a story or essay.

objetive.text: To write a simple description of a room in your house or apartment.

65.explanation: Students will resolve some exercises focusing on houses and living. Practicing these exercises they could use several words and phrases for describing where and how they live, they could be explicit when sharing ideas and opinions in a written or spoken way.

objetive.text: To write a simple description of your house or apartment.

66.explanation: Students will resolve some exercises focusing on houses and living. Practicing these exercises they could use several words and phrases for describing where and how they live, they could be explicit when sharing ideas and opinions in a written or spoken way. Generally to describe our place of living we use the simple present and the structure There is or There are.

objetive.text: To write simple sentences about someone’s work.

67.explanation: In this lesson students will practice some exercises to know more about jobs and occupation. Next you are going to read some expressions and some words to know more about this topic.

objetive.text: To write a simple sentences about someone’s duties.

68.explanation: In this lesson students will practice some exercises to know more about jobs and occupation. Next you are going to read some expressions and some words to know more about this topic. To find out what someone's job is, you can ask, What do you do? Work - What do they do? Where do they work?

objetive.text: To use the definite article to refer to a specific person, thing or situation.

69.explanation: The definite article (THE) is used to refer to a specific ítem, one understood to exist. The definite article (THE) is not used when we refer about things in general.

objetive.text: To use “can” in affirmative, negative and interrogative sentences.

70.explanation: Uses of this modal to show ability.

71.explanation: We use some adverbs to describe how frequently we do an activity. These are called adverbs of frequency.

objetive.text: To make requests and offers with would you like.

72.explanation: The expression “I would like…” is an expression often used to request food items or other things. It´s a form of polite request. The contraction is “I´d like”. It´s considered rude, or not very polite to request items, food or otherwise using (want), it sounds rare to ask for items using (desire).

objetive.text: To understand simple questions in questionnaires on familiar topics.

73.explanation: This is a very common task that you might be asked to talk about in English. It could happen in an interview for college or sometimes a job interview. But it is a very common topic that could take place in an English conversation. You may not have a conversation about your entire daily schedule, but you might have to talk about a small part of your day and what you do. When talking about your daily routine you will only need to use one verb tense. And that is the Simple Present Tense. This is the most basic and easiest of English verb tenses and it is the only one you will need when talking about the things you do every day.

objetive.text: To get the gist of short, simple narratives, with visual support.

74.explanation: The following activities concern with the use of advertisements, which have the potential to develop the skills of communication using visual support. These types of activities could improve students’ cognitive learning skills and initiates them in terms of motivation and creativity thus improving their critical thinking.

objetive.text: To understand simple instructions on everyday equipment.

75.explanation: You often see the imperative form in instruction manuals or when someone tells you how to do something. To make a negative imperative, put “do not” or “don’t” before the verb. (Don’t is more informal than “do not”.) There are often “sequencing” words to show the steps in the process. For example, “firstly”, “secondly” and “finally”. You can also say “after that” instead of “then” and “first” / “second” instead of “firstly” and “secondly”.

objetive.text: To understand simple descriptions of people’s physical appearance.

76.explanation: An adjective is a describing word, the main syntactic role of which is to qualify a noun or noun phrase, giving more information about the object signified. Appearance is defined as the way someone or something looks.

objetive.text: To describe shapes and forms.

77.explanation: It is important to teach students certain basic words about shapes or figures because in this way they can relate some instructions at the time of a practice within the course, a worksheet or in exams, for example when we indicate to them; Circle the correct verb tense. Learning words about basic shapes can also be useful when students try to explain the description of an object and do not know the word in English, another partner or the teacher can help by indicating the correct word.

objetive.text: To identify modal verbs to be used to taking about rules and use them in simple statements.
To understand and use vocabulary related to sports.

79.explanation: There is a growing body of research linking physical activity to improvements in educational performance. This is because sports help students develop character and learn important social and brain skills such as problem solving, resilience, perseverance, confidence, and teamwork. Others researchers also say that by watching or discussing sports, it helps activate the part of the brain involved with playing sports and that helps to understand sports terminology better.

objetive.text: To understand and use words related to shopping.

80.explanation: One of the best ways to teach students shopping vocabulary is to take them on a shopping trip. This may be difficult to handle, but it will be worth the effort. It will give students the opportunity to shop as they normally do, but with an interpreter. The teacher will be there to explain why things happened or why people said what they said. Another way is the students can meet with their teacher at the store with their own money. That way, when the teacher goes shopping, the students will have real questions and can practice the vocabulary.

objetive.text: To give personal information in a written form.

81.explanation: Your job application package is the very first way you present yourself to a potential new employer, and so it is very important that you do it correctly. In this lesson students could practice how to fill a form and to write a text to apply for a job.

objetive.text: To give personal information in a written form.

82.explanation: In this lesson students will write information about themselves using adjectives to describe other people or their own information. Learning how to give personal information in English is crucial when you want to learn a new language and communicate with others. There are many phrases including questions and answers to talk or write about personal information in English. Most of these questions and answers have to do with the Simple Present so that tense should receive priority above the others.

objetive.text: To write a standard greeting on a card.

83.explanation: Knowing how to write good greeting card messages is a skill. Who hasn’t occasionally thought that being a greeting card writer at Hallmark Cards would be a great job? Sitting in your climate-controlled office all day jotting down pearls of wisdom and funny sayings. It sounds like a dream job. But, even writing greeting card messages can be a challenge. You may be under pressure to be witty, romantic, thoughtful, or sympathetic.

objetive.text: To use basic connector like and, but, so, then.

84.explanation: Sometimes students need to organize their ideas to write or talk about a story. There are certain elements that help us explain it more clearly and in a logical sequence, those elements are called sequence connectors. The correct use of these elements will allow students to organize the information they have, in a better way.

85.explanation: “Could I and could you” are used for polite requests, offers and permission.

86.explanation: Whose as question word: We use “Whose” to ask a question about possession. Whose is a possessive pronoun. Use it when you’re asking (or telling) to whom something belongs.

With these exercises they can recognize and use vocabulary related to CV and they could be able to create one for themselves.

There are more than 31 house types from all over the World, each one with its different characteristics. What kind of building do you live in?

So it’s really useful to know how to ask for and understand directions in English so you can reach your destination. It’s also great to be able to give directions yourself to tourists or foreign colleagues.

objetive.text: To write very short, simple sentences about their feelings.

98.explanation: Sometimes you will need to express an emotion such as joy or sorrow to the person you're talking to or maybe writing to. Feelings and emotions are very similar; however, emotions tend to refer to that which is not tangible, while feelings tend to be more tangible.

101.explanation: Going to is not a tense. It is a special structure that we use to talk about the future.

objetive.text: To use (not) many/much with count (countable) and mass (uncountable) nouns respectively.

102.explanation: We use “many” with countable nouns in a negative sentence. We use “much” with uncountable nouns in a negative sentence.

topic.top: WHAT WILL HAPPEN IN  THE FUTURE?

objetive.text: To use “will” to refer about the future.

103.explanation: The simple future tense is the verb tense that refers to the time that is yet to come, a time after the present.

objetive.text: Form the superlative of regular adjectives with “-est”, and of longer regular adjectives with “the most”.

104.explanation: Superlative is the form of an adjective that express that the thing or person being described has more of the particular quality than anything or anyone else of the same type. There are some type of adjectives: One-syllable adjective. Two-syllables ending -y adjective. Two or more syllables adjective. One-syllable consonant-vowel-consonant adjective

objetive.text: To understand short, simple messages on postcards emails and social networks.

105.explanation: A postcard is a piece of thin card, often with a picture on one side, which you can write on and send to people without using an envelope. Sending postcards to friends, family, or loved ones during travel can be a great way to show your affection, as well as giving people an idea of where you are.

objetive.text: To get the gist of short, simple narratives, with visual support.

106.explanation: In this part students will read about Education in Ecuador in order to help them identify main idea statements about sections of a text.

objetive.text: To understand simple instructions on everyday equipment.

107.explanation: When you know how to do something, you have a skill. When you understand how something works, you can alter that knowledge and adapt it for your best uses. If you simply remember how to do something, then all you can do is use it the same way over and over, but if you understand how it works, you can reason about it. Once you can reason about something in your mind you can contemplate why it is the way it is, you can apply your entire creative mind to making the most of it, and you can implement and question improvement – you own it intellectually.

objetive.text: To read simple text and extract factual details.

108.explanation: Students will practice words related to small insects.

objetive.text: o understand and use vocabulary about the environment and pollution.

109.explanation: What do sunlight, water, limestone, and bamboo have in common? They're all natural resources, or useful materials that exist in the environment. Any resource that exists in the natural world — like wood from trees, edible plants found in the forest, or freshwater from a stream — is a natural resource. Some resources, like sunlight, are renewable resources, meaning that they can't be used up. Others, like fossil fuels and deposits of precious metals found in ores, are nonrenewable, meaning that they will one day be used up and can't be replenished.

objetive.text: To identify vocabulary related to Science and Technology.

110.explanation: How much do you depend on technology in your day-to-day life and work? What happens if you lose your phone or your computer crashes? For these exercises students must know vocabulary about Science, Technology and social media.

objetive.text: To understand and use vocabulary related to means of transportation.

111.explanation: Students will use vocabulary about transportation such as plane, bus, car, boat, etc. They also can use some words related to means of transportation and their uses.

objetive.text: To understand and talk about food and words related to it

112.explanation: There are many words you need to learn in order to speak about food, purchase food, cook food, and more. Practicing these exercises you can learn vocabulary about food such as vegetables, fruit and some ingredients for special dishes.

objetive.text: To write short texts about their likes and dislikes using fixed basic expressions.

113.explanation: Learning how to write or talk about likes and dislikes in English is very important since LIKES & DISLIKES is a common topic when you meet new people. To talk about your likes and dislikes, you can use these expressions.

objetive.text: To give an example of something in a very simple text using “like” or “for example”.

114.explanation: In formal writing, like is used as a preposition, telling where, when or how the noun in the sentence is doing whatever it may be doing.

objetive.text: To make simple comparisons between people, places or things.

115.explanation: We use comparative adjectives to show change or make comparisons. We use than when we want to compare one thing with another. When we want to describe how something or someone changes we can use two comparatives with and. We often use the with comparative adjectives to show that one thing depends on another.

objetive.text: To ask for personal information in a written form.

116.explanation: Learning how to ask and give personal information in English is crucial when you want to learn a new language and communicate with others. There are many phrases including questions and answers to talk about personal information in English. Most of these questions are Wh- questions to talk about personal information in English. We use question words to ask certain types of questions. We often refer to these words ahs WH words because they include WH (for example, Why, How). The answer for these questions cannot be yes or no.

topic.top: WAITING FOR YOU, I MADE SOME COFFEE

objetive.text: To identify the use of participle clauses  is a subordinate clause which  begins with a participle. They usually show things like event order, time, cause and effect.

308.explanation: This is an activity where students are going to learn about participle clause. These clauses are used to avoid making sentences overly complicated. They are used mainly in written English and they allow us to convey a great deal of information in a shorter form.
